passages.text: When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people conspired against Jesus to put Him to death.
passages.sermon:
Morning arrived.
All the chief priests gathered.
All the elders of the people gathered.
They met together.
They made a plan against Jesus.
They decided to put Jesus to death.
passages.original: Πρωΐας δὲ γενομένης συμβούλιον ἔλαβον πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὥστε θανατῶσαι αὐτόν

passages.text: They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and elders arrested Jesus.
They tied Jesus up.
They took Jesus away from where He was.
They brought Jesus to Pilate.
Pilate was the Roman governor.
They handed Jesus over to Pilate.
passages.original: καὶ δήσαντες αὐτὸν ἀπήγαγον καὶ παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ τῷ ἡγεμόνι

passages.text: When Judas, who had betrayed Him, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was filled with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.
passages.sermon:
Judas was the disciple who betrayed Jesus.
Judas saw that the leaders condemned Jesus.
Judas felt deep regret.
Judas returned the thirty pieces of silver.
Judas gave the silver back to the chief priests and elders.
passages.original: Τότε ἰδὼν Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ὅτι κατεκρίθη μεταμεληθεὶς ἔστρεψεν τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ πρεσβυτέροις

passages.text: “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood,” he said. “What is that to us?” they replied. “You bear the responsibility.”
passages.sermon:
Judas had betrayed Jesus.
Jesus was innocent.
Judas said, “I have sinned.”
He said, “I betrayed innocent blood.”
The chief priests and elders answered him.
They said, “What is that to us?”
They said, “You are responsible.”
passages.original: λέγων Ἥμαρτον παραδοὺς αἷμα ἀθῷον Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς σὺ ὄψῃ

passages.text: So Judas threw the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
passages.sermon:
Judas was the disciple who betrayed Jesus.
Judas took the thirty pieces of silver.
He threw the silver into the temple.
Judas left the temple.
He went away.
Judas hanged himself.
passages.original: Καὶ ῥίψας τὰ ἀργύρια εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἀνεχώρησεν καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπήγξατο

passages.text: The chief priests picked up the pieces of silver and said, “It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money.”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests took the pieces of silver.
They spoke about the money.
They said, “We cannot put this money into the temple treasury.”
They explained the reason.
They said, “This money paid for blood.”
They called it blood money.
They said it is not lawful to use it for the treasury.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια εἶπαν Οὐκ ἔξεστιν βαλεῖν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν κορβανᾶν ἐπεὶ τιμὴ αἵματός ἐστιν

passages.text: After conferring together, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests took the silver coins.
They talked together and made a decision.
They used the silver coins to buy a field.
This field belonged to a potter.
They bought the field to bury foreigners there.
passages.original: συμβούλιον δὲ λαβόντες ἠγόρασαν ἐξ αὐτῶν τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως εἰς ταφὴν τοῖς ξένοις

passages.text: That is why it has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
passages.sermon: The people called that field the Field of Blood.\r\nThey still use this name today.\r\nThey gave it this name because the chief priests bought the field with blood money.
passages.original: διὸ ἐκλήθη ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκεῖνος Ἀγρὸς αἵματος ἕως τῆς σήμερον

passages.text: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on Him by the people of Israel, and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord had commanded me.”
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet.
God spoke through Jeremiah.
God gave Jeremiah a message about the Messiah.
The people of Israel set a price on the Messiah.
They valued Him at thirty pieces of silver.
They took the thirty pieces of silver.
They gave the silver for the potter’s field.
They did this as the Lord commanded.
This fulfilled what God had spoken through Jeremiah.
passages.original: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος Καὶ ἔλαβον τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια τὴν τιμὴν τοῦ τετιμημένου ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ καὶ ἔδωκαν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως καθὰ συνέταξέν μοι Κύριος

passages.text: Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, who questioned Him: “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood in front of the governor.
The governor spoke to Jesus.
The governor asked, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answered the governor.
Jesus said, “You say so.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ ἡγεμὼν λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔφη Σὺ λέγεις

passages.text: And when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He gave no answer.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the governor.
The chief priests accused Jesus.
The elders also accused Jesus.
Jesus did not answer them.
Jesus remained silent.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο

passages.text: Then Pilate asked Him, “Do You not hear how many charges they are bringing against You?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
\r\nJesus stood before Pilate.
\r\nPilate spoke to Jesus.
\r\nPilate asked Jesus a question.
\r\nPilate said, “Do you not hear?”
\r\nPilate said, “They are bringing many charges against you.”
\r\nPilate asked, “Do you not hear how many charges they are bringing against you?”
passages.original: Τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος Οὐκ ἀκούεις πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν

passages.text: But Jesus gave no answer, not even to a single charge, much to the governor’s amazement.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the governor, Pilate.
The chief priests and elders accused Jesus.
Pilate asked Jesus about the charges.
Jesus did not answer Pilate.
Jesus did not reply to a single accusation.
The governor was very amazed.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲ ἓν ῥῆμα ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν

passages.text: Now it was the governor’s custom at the feast to release to the crowd a prisoner of their choosing.
passages.sermon: The governor had a custom during the feast.\r\nHe released one prisoner to the crowd at that time.\r\nThe crowd chose which prisoner the governor would release.
passages.original: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν εἰώθει ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀπολύειν ἕνα τῷ ὄχλῳ δέσμιον ὃν ἤθελον

passages.text: At that time they were holding a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.
passages.sermon:
At that time, the people held a prisoner.
This prisoner was well-known.
His name was Barabbas.
passages.original: εἶχον δὲ τότε δέσμιον ἐπίσημον λεγόμενον Βαραββᾶν

passages.text: So when the crowd had assembled, Pilate asked them, “Which one do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
He had a custom during the feast.
He would release one prisoner to the crowd.
The crowd gathered together.
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
He asked them a question.
He said, "Which one do you want me to release to you?"
He gave them two choices.
He said, "Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"
passages.original: συνηγμένων οὖν αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος Τίνα θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἢ Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον Χριστόν

passages.text: For he knew it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over to him.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate knew something important.
The leaders handed Jesus over to Pilate.
They did this because they envied Jesus.
Pilate understood their motive was envy.
passages.original: ᾔδει γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παρέδωκαν αὐτόν

passages.text: While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him this message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man, for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate sat on the judgment seat.
Pilate’s wife sent a message to him.
She said, “Have nothing to do with that innocent man.”
She called Jesus innocent.
She said, “I have suffered greatly today in a dream because of him.”
passages.original: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ λέγουσα Μηδὲν σοὶ καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐκείνῳ πολλὰ γὰρ ἔπαθον σήμερον κατ’ ὄναρ δι’ αὐτόν

passages.text: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the elders acted together.
They spoke to the crowds.
They persuaded the crowds.
They told the crowds to ask for Barabbas.
They wanted the crowds to demand Barabbas’s release.
They also wanted Jesus to be put to death.
They persuaded the crowds to ask for Jesus to be killed.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεισαν τοὺς ὄχλους ἵνα αἰτήσωνται τὸν Βαραββᾶν τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν ἀπολέσωσιν

passages.text: “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” asked the governor. “Barabbas,” they replied.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?”
The crowd answered him.
They said, “Barabbas.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἡγεμὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τίνα θέλετε ἀπὸ τῶν δύο ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Τὸν Βαραββᾶν

passages.text: “What then should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” Pilate asked. They all answered, “Crucify Him!”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
Pilate asked a question about Jesus.
Jesus was called the Christ.
Pilate said, “What should I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?”
All the people answered Pilate.
They said, “Crucify Him!”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος Τί οὖν ποιήσω Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον Χριστόν Λέγουσιν πάντες Σταυρωθήτω

passages.text: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
Pilate asked, “Why?”
Pilate said, “What evil has Jesus done?”
The crowd did not answer Pilate’s question.
The crowd shouted even louder.
The crowd said, “Crucify Him!”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν Οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραζον λέγοντες Σταυρωθήτω

passages.text: When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that instead a riot was breaking out, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd. “I am innocent of this man’s blood,” he said. “You bear the responsibility.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate saw that he could not change the crowd’s mind.
Pilate saw that a riot was starting.
Pilate took water.
Pilate washed his hands in front of the crowd.
Pilate spoke to the people.
Pilate said, “I am innocent of this man’s blood.”
Pilate said, “You are responsible.”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ὅτι οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον θόρυβος γίνεται λαβὼν ὕδωρ ἀπενίψατο τὰς χεῖρας ἀπέναντι τοῦ ὄχλου λέγων Ἀθῷός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τούτου ὑμεῖς ὄψεσθε

passages.text: All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children!”
passages.sermon:
All the people spoke together.
They answered Pilate.
They said, “Let His blood be on us.
Let His blood be on our children.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πᾶς ὁ λαὸς εἶπεν Τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν

passages.text: So Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate released Barabbas to the people.
Pilate ordered Jesus to be flogged.
Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified.
passages.original: Τότε ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας παρέδωκεν ἵνα σταυρωθῇ

passages.text: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium and gathered the whole company around Him.
passages.sermon:
The governor’s soldiers took Jesus.
They led Jesus into the Praetorium.
The Praetorium was the governor’s headquarters.
The soldiers gathered the whole company around Jesus.
Many soldiers surrounded Him.
passages.original: Τότε οἱ στρατιῶται τοῦ ἡγεμόνος παραλαβόντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον συνήγαγον ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν

passages.text: They stripped Him and put a scarlet robe on Him.
passages.sermon: The soldiers took Jesus.\r\nThey removed His clothes.\r\nThey put a scarlet robe on Him.
passages.original: καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν χλαμύδα κοκκίνην περιέθηκαν αὐτῷ

passages.text: And they twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on His head. They put a staff in His right hand and knelt down before Him to mock Him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
passages.sermon:
The governor’s soldiers took Jesus.
They twisted a crown from thorns.
They placed the crown of thorns on Jesus’ head.
They put a staff in Jesus’ right hand.
They knelt down in front of Jesus.
They mocked Jesus.
They said, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
passages.original: καὶ πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ κάλαμον ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ καὶ γονυπετήσαντες ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες Χαῖρε Βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: Then they spit on Him and took the staff and struck Him on the head repeatedly.
passages.sermon: The soldiers spit on Jesus.\r\nThey took the staff from Him.\r\nThey struck Jesus on the head with the staff again and again.
passages.original: καὶ ἐμπτύσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν ἔλαβον τὸν κάλαμον καὶ ἔτυπτον εἰς τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: After they had mocked Him, they removed the robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him away to crucify Him.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers mocked Jesus.
They took off the robe from Jesus.
They put Jesus’ own clothes back on Him.
They led Jesus away.
They led Him away to crucify Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν χλαμύδα καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σταυρῶσαι

passages.text: Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers led Jesus away to be crucified.
They found a man on the road.
This man came from Cyrene.
His name was Simon.
The soldiers forced Simon to carry the cross of Jesus.
passages.original: Ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ εὗρον ἄνθρωπον Κυρηναῖον ὀνόματι Σίμωνα τοῦτον ἠγγάρευσαν ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And when they came to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull, they offered Him wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, He refused to drink it.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers led Jesus to a place called Golgotha.
Golgotha means The Place of the Skull.
At Golgotha, the soldiers offered Jesus wine mixed with gall.
Jesus tasted the wine mixed with gall.
Jesus refused to drink it.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Γολγοθᾶ ὅ ἐστιν κρανίου τόπος λεγόμενος ἔδωκαν αὐτῷ πιεῖν οἶνον μετὰ χολῆς μεμιγμένον καὶ γευσάμενος οὐκ ἠθέλησεν πιεῖν

passages.text: When they had crucified Him, they divided up His garments by casting lots.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers crucified Jesus.
They took His garments.
They divided His garments among themselves.
They cast lots to decide who would get each piece.
passages.original: Σταυρώσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ βάλλοντες κλῆρον

passages.text: And sitting down, they kept watch over Him there.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers sat down.
They watched Jesus there.
They kept guard over Him at the place called Golgotha.
Golgotha means The Place of the Skull.
Jesus was being crucified.
passages.original: καὶ καθήμενοι ἐτήρουν αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ

passages.text: Above His head they posted the written charge against Him: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers crucified Jesus.
They placed a sign above His head.
The sign showed the charge against Him.
The sign said: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπάνω τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ τὴν αἰτίαν αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένην ΟΥΤΟΣ ΕΣΤΙΝ ΙΗΣΟΥΣ Ο ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΤΩΝ ΙΟΥΔΑΙΩΝ

passages.text: Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right hand and the other on His left.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers crucified Jesus.
They crucified two robbers with Him.
One robber was on Jesus’ right side.
The other robber was on Jesus’ left side.
passages.original: Τότε σταυροῦνται σὺν αὐτῷ δύο λῃσταί εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων

passages.text: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
People walked by Him.
These people insulted Jesus.
They shook their heads at Him.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “You said you would destroy the temple.
You said you would build it again in three days.
Save yourself now.
If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ λέγοντες Ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις οἰκοδομῶν σῶσον σεαυτόν εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ κατάβηθι ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ

passages.text: In the same way, the chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself. He is the King of Israel! Let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests, scribes, and elders stood near the cross.
They mocked Jesus.
They spoke to each other about Him.
They said, “He saved other people.
He cannot save Himself.
He is the King of Israel.
Let Him come down now from the cross.
Then we will believe in Him.”
passages.original: Ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων ἔλεγον Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι Βασιλεὺς Ἰσραήλ ἐστιν καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ πιστεύσομεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus hung on the cross.
The chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him.
They said, “He trusts in God.
Let God deliver Him now, if God wants Him.
He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
passages.original: πέποιθεν ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν ῥυσάσθω νῦν εἰ θέλει αὐτόν εἶπεν γὰρ ὅτι Θεοῦ εἰμι Υἱός

passages.text: In the same way, even the robbers who were crucified with Him berated Him.
passages.sermon: Two robbers were crucified with Jesus.\r\nThese robbers insulted Jesus.\r\nThey mocked Him in the same way as the others.
passages.original: Τὸ δ’ αὐτὸ καὶ οἱ λῃσταὶ οἱ συσταυρωθέντες σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν

passages.text: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
passages.sermon: From the sixth hour darkness covered all the land.\r\nThis darkness lasted until the ninth hour.
passages.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ ἕκτης ὥρας σκότος ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης

passages.text: About the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was crucified.
He was on the cross.
About the ninth hour, Jesus cried out.
He used a loud voice.
He said, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?”
This means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
passages.original: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἐνάτην ὥραν ἀνεβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων Ἠλὶ ἠλὶ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Θεέ μου θεέ μου ἵνα‿ τί με ἐγκατέλιπες

passages.text: When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “He is calling Elijah.”
passages.sermon:
Some people stood near the cross.
They heard Jesus cry out.
They listened to His words.
They said, “He is calling Elijah.”
passages.original: Τινὲς δὲ τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ οὗτος

passages.text: One of them quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink.
passages.sermon:
One man stood among the people near Jesus.
He saw what was happening.
He quickly ran to get a sponge.
He took the sponge in his hand.
He filled the sponge with sour wine.
He put the sponge on a reed.
He lifted the reed up to Jesus.
He gave Jesus a drink from the sponge.
passages.original: καὶ εὐθέως δραμὼν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν καὶ λαβὼν σπόγγον πλήσας τε ὄξους καὶ περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν

passages.text: But the others said, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.”
passages.sermon:
Some people stood near Jesus as He was on the cross.
They heard Him speak.
Other people there spoke to each other.
They said, “Leave Him alone.”
They said, “Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἔλεγον Ἄφες ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας σώσων αὐτόν

passages.text: When Jesus had cried out again in a loud voice, He yielded up His spirit.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
Jesus cried out again.
He used a loud voice.
Jesus gave up His spirit.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἀφῆκεν τὸ πνεῦμα

passages.text: At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
passages.sermon:
At that moment, something happened in the temple.
The veil in the temple tore in two.
The tear started at the top and went down to the bottom.
The earth shook.
The rocks split apart.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη ἀπ’ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω εἰς δύο καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐσείσθη καὶ αἱ πέτραι ἐσχίσθησαν

passages.text: The tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
passages.sermon:
The tombs opened.
Many saints had died.
God raised the bodies of these saints.
These saints had fallen asleep in death.
God made them alive again.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ μνημεῖα ἀνεῴχθησαν καὶ πολλὰ σώματα τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἁγίων ἠγέρθησαν

passages.text: After Jesus’ resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus rose from the dead.
Many saints had died before.
God raised these saints to life.
After Jesus’ resurrection, these saints left their tombs.
They entered the holy city.
They appeared to many people.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκ τῶν μνημείων μετὰ τὴν ἔγερσιν αὐτοῦ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν καὶ ἐνεφανίσθησαν πολλοῖς

passages.text: When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and all that had happened, they were terrified and said, “Truly this was the Son of God.”
passages.sermon:
A centurion stood near Jesus.
Other men stood with the centurion.
These men guarded Jesus.
They saw an earthquake.
They saw everything that happened.
They became very afraid.
They spoke together.
They said, “Truly, this was the Son of God.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἑκατόνταρχος καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ τηροῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδόντες τὸν σεισμὸν καὶ τὰ γενόμενα ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα λέγοντες Ἀληθῶς Θεοῦ Υἱὸς ἦν οὗτος

passages.text: And many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him.
passages.sermon:
Many women were there.
They watched from a distance.
These women had followed Jesus.
They came with Him from Galilee.
They served Jesus.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ γυναῖκες πολλαὶ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι αἵτινες ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας διακονοῦσαι αὐτῷ

passages.text: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
passages.sermon:
Many women watched from a distance.
They had followed Jesus from Galilee.
They had served Jesus.
Mary Magdalene was there.
Mary the mother of James and Joseph was there.
The mother of the sons of Zebedee was there.
passages.original: ἐν αἷς ἦν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνή καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσὴφ μήτηρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου

passages.text: When it was evening, there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, who himself was a disciple of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
A man named Joseph came from Arimathea.
Joseph was rich.
Joseph was a disciple of Jesus.
This happened in the evening.
passages.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἦλθεν ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας τοὔνομα Ἰωσήφ ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐμαθητεύθη τῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus, and Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a rich man from Arimathea.
Joseph was a disciple of Jesus.
Joseph went to Pilate.
Joseph asked Pilate for the body of Jesus.
Pilate gave an order.
Pilate ordered that the body of Jesus be given to Joseph.
passages.original: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τότε ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐκέλευσεν ἀποδοθῆναι

passages.text: So Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a great stone across the entrance to the tomb and went away.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a rich man from Arimathea.
Joseph was a disciple of Jesus.
Joseph took the body of Jesus.
He wrapped the body in a clean linen cloth.
He placed the body in his own new tomb.
Joseph had cut this tomb into the rock.
He rolled a large stone across the entrance of the tomb.
Joseph went away.
passages.original: καὶ λαβὼν τὸ σῶμα ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ ἐν σινδόνι καθαρᾷ καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸ ἐν τῷ καινῷ αὐτοῦ μνημείῳ ὃ ἐλατόμησεν ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ καὶ προσκυλίσας λίθον μέγαν τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπῆλθεν

passages.text: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there opposite the tomb.
passages.sermon: Mary Magdalene was there.\r\nThe other Mary was also there.\r\nThey sat across from the tomb.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία καθήμεναι ἀπέναντι τοῦ τάφου

passages.text: The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees assembled before Pilate.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the Pharisees were Jewish religious leaders.
Preparation Day was the day before the Sabbath.
The next day came after Preparation Day.
On that day, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered together.
They went to Pilate.
Pilate was the Roman governor.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἥτις ἐστὶν μετὰ τὴν Παρασκευήν συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς Πιλᾶτον

passages.text: “Sir,” they said, “we remember that while He was alive that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the Pharisees spoke to Pilate.
They said, “Sir, we remember something.”
They remembered what Jesus said while He was still alive.
They called Jesus a deceiver.
They said, “That deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’”
passages.original: λέγοντες Κύριε ἐμνήσθημεν ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὁ πλάνος εἶπεν ἔτι ζῶν Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγείρομαι

passages.text: So give the order that the tomb be secured until the third day. Otherwise, His disciples may come and steal Him away and tell the people He has risen from the dead. And this last deception would be worse than the first.”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and Pharisees spoke to Pilate.
They asked Pilate to give an order.
They wanted the tomb to be secured until the third day.
They feared something might happen.
They said, “His disciples may come.
They may steal His body.
They may tell the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’
This last deception would be worse than the first.”
passages.original: κέλευσον οὖν ἀσφαλισθῆναι τὸν τάφον ἕως τῆς τρίτης ἡμέρας μή‿ ποτε ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κλέψωσιν αὐτὸν καὶ εἴπωσιν τῷ λαῷ Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἐσχάτη πλάνη χείρων τῆς πρώτης

passages.text: “You have a guard,” Pilate said. “Go, make the tomb as secure as you know how.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the chief priests and Pharisees.
Pilate said, “You have a guard.”
Pilate told them, “Go.”
Pilate commanded them, “Make the tomb as secure as you know how.”
passages.original: Ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος Ἔχετε κουστωδίαν ὑπάγετε ἀσφαλίσασθε ὡς οἴδατε

passages.text: So they went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone and posting the guard.
passages.sermon:
The guards went to the tomb.
They sealed the stone at the entrance.
They made the tomb secure.
They stayed there to guard it.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ πορευθέντες ἠσφαλίσαντο τὸν τάφον σφραγίσαντες τὸν λίθον μετὰ τῆς κουστωδίας
